associations.rationale: This constructs the balancing morphism from the copower involving B tensor X to the copower involving X, but the displayed type does not expose the stated difference-of-actions formula or its cokernel property.
This is the object-level balanced-tensor construction, but its displayed type is opaque about the cokernel presentation required in the source statement.
This packages balanced tensoring as a functor from finite B-modules to the category, a construction needed for G, while the displayed type does not state its action X maps to P tensor_B X.

The displayed type proves that the kernel of the opaque `evaluationApp` morphism is zero, but does not expose that morphism as `ξ.app Y`; it therefore provides contextual evidence for the K = 0 step rather than directly stating part (iii).

This supplies an equivalence between the category and finite modules over End(P)^op, but the displayed type does not identify its functors with the particular F and G whose quasi-inverse relationship the problem asks to prove.

The copower-Hom linear equivalence is an auxiliary adjunction-style identification used in the construction and proof, not one of the problem's stated natural isomorphisms between F, G, and identity functors.
This defines the module action map on X used to form the balancing relation, so it is a prerequisite construction rather than a direct statement of parts (i)-(iii).
The displayed functor isomorphism states that composing balanced tensor with the Hom(P,-) functor is naturally isomorphic to the identity on finite B-modules, directly matching part (i).
For every object Y, this directly asserts that the component of the natural transformation xi is an epimorphism, formalizing the requested surjectivity in part (ii).
The formal type directly states that the natural transformation xi from G composed with F to the identity is an isomorphism, which is the conclusion of part (iii).
This constructs the action morphism from the copower of P by its endomorphism algebra to P, an ingredient in the balanced relation rather than a requested conclusion.
This directly constructs the natural morphism xi from the composite of the Hom and balanced-tensor functors to the identity functor, matching the construction requested in part (ii).
